project.name: treetracker-field-data
project.description: Field data service that owns raw tree tracking data uploaded from treetracker app devices. It ingests raw captures, tracks field sessions and device movement, registers devices and wallets, and publishes domain events to downstream systems while dual-writing to the legacy treetracker database during migration.

nodes.name: Raw Capture Ingestion
nodes.summary: Owns the raw tree captures that treetracker app devices upload. It creates, queries, verifies and rejects captures, coordinating dual writes to the field-data and legacy databases and emitting domain events for each action.

businessRules: A capture write spans the main field-data database and the legacy database in one atomic unit; failure rolls back both
Each capture create or reject raises a matching domain event (capture-created / capture-rejected)
A capture references its session, wallet registration and device configuration
crossDomainInteractions: Publishes capture events to Domain Events & Messaging
Dual-writes legacy tree records via Legacy Database Bridging
Joins Session, Wallet Registration and Device Configuration data on read

nodes.name: Session & Track Tracking
nodes.summary: Records field capture sessions, session segments, and device movement tracks. It provides transactional creation and paginated queries for sessions and tracks that captures reference.

businessRules: Sessions carry an organization id used to bridge captures to organizations
Session and track creation run inside a database transaction with rollback on failure
crossDomainInteractions: Provides session context that Raw Capture Ingestion joins on read

nodes.name: Device Configuration
nodes.summary: Registers and queries the configuration of treetracker devices in the field. Configurations are created transactionally and joined into captures for provenance.

businessRules: Device configuration creation is wrapped in a database transaction
crossDomainInteractions: Supplies device metadata joined into Raw Capture Ingestion reads

nodes.name: Wallet Registration
nodes.summary: Registers the wallets that captures are attributed to and lets clients query them. Creation is idempotent, returning the existing record on duplicate, and is backfilled from legacy data via ETL.

businessRules: Creating a wallet registration is idempotent: a duplicate returns the existing record
Creation runs inside a transaction that rolls back on error
crossDomainInteractions: Provides wallet attribution joined into Raw Capture Ingestion reads
Backfilled from legacy data by Legacy Database Bridging ETL

nodes.name: Domain Events & Messaging
nodes.summary: Implements the event-sourcing outbox and RabbitMQ messaging that carry capture events out of the service and back in for processing. It publishes, consumes, and replays domain events with at-least-once delivery.

businessRules: Domain events are persisted to a partitioned outbox table before and after publication
Incoming events are processed inside a transactional session; failure rolls back and re-queues via republish/nack recovery
Stored events can be replayed by re-publishing or re-applying handlers for recovery
crossDomainInteractions: Receives capture-created and capture-rejected events from Raw Capture Ingestion
Reprocesses captures on consume and replay

nodes.name: Legacy Database Bridging
nodes.summary: Bridges field-data records into the legacy treetracker main database during migration. It maps captures to legacy tree, planter and attribute records and backfills wallet registrations and session ids from legacy data.

businessRules: Each new capture is dual-written as a legacy tree with its planter lookup and tree attributes
Rejecting a capture also rejects the corresponding legacy tree via the legacy API
crossDomainInteractions: Persists legacy trees on behalf of Raw Capture Ingestion
Backfills Wallet Registration records from legacy data

nodes.name: Create Raw Capture
nodes.summary: Accepts a new raw tree capture from a device, persists it to the field-data and legacy databases in a dual transaction, and publishes a capture-created event.

nodes.name: Reject Raw Capture
nodes.summary: Marks an existing raw capture as rejected, rejects the corresponding legacy tree, and publishes a capture-rejected event.

nodes.name: Query Raw Captures
nodes.summary: Returns raw captures as a paginated list with prev/next links or as a single capture by id.

nodes.name: Create Session
nodes.summary: Validates and persists a new field capture session inside a database transaction.

nodes.name: Query Sessions
nodes.summary: Returns sessions joined with wallet and device configuration data as a paginated list or a single session by id.

nodes.name: Track Device Movement
nodes.summary: Creates device movement track records transactionally and returns them as a paginated list or single track by id.

nodes.name: Register Device Configuration
nodes.summary: Validates and creates a device configuration record inside a database transaction.

nodes.name: Query Device Configurations
nodes.summary: Returns device configurations as a paginated list with total count and prev/next links or a single configuration by id.

nodes.name: Create Wallet Registration
nodes.summary: Validates and idempotently creates a wallet registration inside a transaction, returning the existing record on duplicate.

nodes.name: Query Wallet Registrations
nodes.summary: Returns wallet registrations as a paginated list with prev/next links or a single registration by id.

nodes.name: Publish Capture Event
nodes.summary: Raises a domain event on a model, persists it to the outbox, and publishes it to RabbitMQ for downstream consumers.

nodes.name: Consume Capture Event
nodes.summary: Subscribes to the capture-creation queue and processes incoming events inside a transactional session, updating domain event state on success or rollback.

nodes.name: Replay Domain Events
nodes.summary: Loads stored domain events and re-publishes them to the queue or re-applies their handlers for recovery.

nodes.name: Dual-Write Legacy Tree
nodes.summary: Maps a new capture into legacy tree records and persists them with a planter lookup and bulk tree-attribute inserts into the legacy database.

nodes.name: Backfill From Legacy ETL
nodes.summary: One-off ETL that generates legacy session ids and builds wallet registration rows from legacy data during migration.

nodes.name: Validate capture payload
nodes.summary: Validates the incoming capture request body against the Joi schema in the raw capture handler.

nodes.name: Begin dual transactions
nodes.summary: RawCaptureService opens transactional sessions on both the main and legacy databases to coordinate an atomic write.

nodes.name: Persist raw capture
nodes.summary: RawCaptureRepository inserts the raw_capture row, resolving session, wallet registration and device configuration references.

nodes.name: Write legacy tree
nodes.summary: LegacyTree maps the capture into legacy tree records and writes them to the legacy database.

nodes.name: Raise capture-created event
nodes.summary: The RawCapture model raises a capture-created domain event, persisted to the outbox by the event repository.

nodes.name: Publish capture-created message
nodes.summary: QueueService publishes the capture-created message to RabbitMQ.

nodes.name: Commit transactions
nodes.summary: RawCaptureService commits both database transactions, rolling back both on any failure.

nodes.name: Validate reject request
nodes.summary: rawCaptureRejectPatch validates the request parameters for the capture to reject.

nodes.name: Mark capture rejected
nodes.summary: RawCaptureService updates the capture status to rejected through the RawCapture model.

nodes.name: Reject legacy tree
nodes.summary: LegacyAPIService issues a PATCH to the legacy tree API to reject the legacy tree for its organization.

nodes.name: Raise capture-rejected event
nodes.summary: The RawCapture model raises a capture-rejected domain event.

nodes.name: Publish capture-rejected message
nodes.summary: QueueService publishes the capture-rejected message to RabbitMQ.

nodes.name: Validate query params
nodes.summary: rawCaptureGet validates query parameters and applies filter/limit options.

nodes.name: Fetch paginated captures
nodes.summary: RawCaptureRepository reads captures with left joins to session, wallet registration and device configuration.

nodes.name: Build prev/next links
nodes.summary: generatePrevAndNext builds pagination links from the request, limit and offset.

nodes.name: Fetch single capture
nodes.summary: rawCaptureSingleGet fetches a single raw capture by id through RawCaptureService.

nodes.name: Validate session payload
nodes.summary: sessionPost validates the session creation payload against the Joi schema.

nodes.name: Begin transaction
nodes.summary: SessionService opens a transactional session on the field-data database.

nodes.name: Persist session
nodes.summary: SessionModel creates the session row through SessionRepository.

nodes.name: Commit transaction
nodes.summary: SessionService commits the transaction, rolling back on failure.

nodes.name: Validate query params
nodes.summary: sessionGet validates query parameters and applies filter/limit options.

nodes.name: Fetch paginated sessions
nodes.summary: SessionRepository builds join and count queries across wallet_registration and device_configuration tables.

nodes.name: Build prev/next links
nodes.summary: generatePrevAndNext builds pagination links for the session list.

nodes.name: Fetch single session
nodes.summary: sessionSingleGet validates the id path parameter and returns the matching session.

nodes.name: Create track
nodes.summary: TrackService wraps track creation in a database transaction with rollback on failure.

nodes.name: List tracks
nodes.summary: trackGet validates query params and returns a paginated list of tracks with prev/next links.

nodes.name: Fetch single track
nodes.summary: trackSingleGet fetches a single track by id via TrackService.

nodes.name: Validate configuration body
nodes.summary: deviceConfigurationPost validates the request body against the Joi schema.

nodes.name: Begin transaction
nodes.summary: DeviceConfigurationService opens a transactional session for the write.

nodes.name: Persist configuration
nodes.summary: The DeviceConfiguration model creates the configuration row through its repository.

nodes.name: Commit transaction
nodes.summary: DeviceConfigurationService commits the transaction, rolling back on error.

nodes.name: Validate query params
nodes.summary: deviceConfigurationGet validates query parameters for the list request.

nodes.name: Fetch paginated configurations
nodes.summary: The DeviceConfiguration model retrieves a paginated list with total count via its repository.

nodes.name: Build prev/next links
nodes.summary: generatePrevAndNext builds pagination navigation links for the configuration list.

nodes.name: Fetch single configuration
nodes.summary: deviceConfigurationSingleGet validates the id path parameter and returns one configuration.

nodes.name: Validate registration body
nodes.summary: walletRegistrationPost validates the request body against the Joi schema.

nodes.name: Begin transaction
nodes.summary: WalletRegistrationService opens a transactional session for the write.

nodes.name: Idempotent create
nodes.summary: The WalletRegistration model creates the registration and returns the existing record on a duplicate to keep the operation idempotent.

nodes.name: Commit transaction
nodes.summary: WalletRegistrationService commits the transaction, rolling back on error.

nodes.name: Validate query params
nodes.summary: walletRegistrationGet validates query parameters for the list request.

nodes.name: Fetch paginated registrations
nodes.summary: The WalletRegistration model retrieves a paginated list through its repository.

nodes.name: Build prev/next links
nodes.summary: generatePrevAndNext builds pagination navigation links for the registration list.

nodes.name: Fetch single registration
nodes.summary: walletRegistrationSingleGet fetches a single wallet registration by id.

nodes.name: Raise domain event
nodes.summary: A domain model raises a domain event describing the capture action.

nodes.name: Persist to outbox
nodes.summary: EventRepository inserts the domain event into the partitioned outbox table.

nodes.name: Publish to RabbitMQ
nodes.summary: QueueService publishes the event message through the RabbitMQ broker wrapper.

nodes.name: Mark event sent
nodes.summary: The DomainEvent state is updated to sent once published.

nodes.name: Subscribe to queue
nodes.summary: EventHandlerService registers queue subscribers on the capture-creation queue.

nodes.name: Process in transaction
nodes.summary: EventHandlerService processes the incoming message inside a transactional session.

nodes.name: Update event state
nodes.summary: The domain event handled state is updated on successful processing.

nodes.name: Ack or rollback
nodes.summary: On success the message is acknowledged; on failure the transaction rolls back and the broker republishes or dead-letters the message.

nodes.name: Receive replay request
nodes.summary: The replay event handler receives the replay POST request and forwards it to ReplayEventService.

nodes.name: Load stored events
nodes.summary: ReplayEventService loads the stored domain events from the outbox via EventRepository.

nodes.name: Republish or re-apply
nodes.summary: ReplayEventService re-publishes the events to the queue or re-applies the event handlers for recovery.

nodes.name: Map capture to legacy tree
nodes.summary: LegacyTree builds a frozen legacy tree entity from the capture.

nodes.name: Lookup planter
nodes.summary: LegacyPlanterRepository finds the legacy planter by phone or email identifier.

nodes.name: Insert legacy tree
nodes.summary: LegacyTreeRepository inserts the tree row into the legacy database via a raw parameterized query.

nodes.name: Bulk-insert tree attributes
nodes.summary: LegacyTreeAttributeRepository bulk-inserts tree attribute rows concurrently.

nodes.name: Generate legacy session ids
nodes.summary: The ETL script derives deterministic legacy session ids for backfill.

nodes.name: Build wallet registrations from legacy
nodes.summary: The ETL SQL creates wallet_registration rows from legacy data.

edges.description: Capture creation and rejection raise capture-created and capture-rejected domain events that are published and consumed through messaging.
Each capture write dual-writes a corresponding legacy tree, and capture rejection rejects the legacy tree.
Captures reference and join session data on read.
Captures reference and join wallet registration data for attribution.
Captures reference and join device configuration data for provenance.
Consuming and replaying capture events reprocesses captures within transactional sessions.
ETL backfills wallet registration records from legacy data during migration.
